parsed.explanation: Parent regime supplies real traveler-facing exposures: sex-binary document scrutiny, visa refusal on sex-discrepancy grounds, foreign travel advisories, a federal ban on gender-congruent access to government-funded single-sex facilities (airports included), and documented custody harm (conversion-therapy policy, immigration-detention abuse). The division starts at that line and moves up: public-accommodations ban since 2006 (visitor-facing), an operating shield law expressly covering travelling patients, gender-identity hate-crime penalties, gender-neutral single-occupancy restrooms, protected facility access, no bathroom ban, and a 'Most Protective' legislative record. Those mitigations are documented in force, not paper. But entry screening and federal facilities remain outside state control, custody-placement practice is undocumented, and enforcement data is thin—so the score sits mid-reduced-risk, above the parent average but held down by universal federal exposures.
